prose_slots: Short-time spectra of the reference $u$ and measured actuator displacement $y$ provide frequency-resolved evidence for estimating the margin in {eq:bncf} as the specimen degrades. These signals are transformed in overlapping windows during the experiment, and their spectra are averaged across updates. Each estimate uses the most recent $T_w=0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ of data and is updated every $\Delta t=0.125\,\mathrm{s}$, giving 75% overlap between consecutive windows. At $f_s=2048\,\mathrm{Hz}$, each window contains $N=f_sT_w=1024$ samples and has a Fourier-bin spacing of 2 Hz. where $w[r]=\tfrac{1}{2}\{1-\cos[2\pi r/(N-1)]\}$ is the Hann window and $\omega_m=2\pi mf_s/N$ is the angular frequency at bin $m$. At each bin, the transforms $U_n$ and $Y_n$ give the instantaneous auto- and cross-spectra

The frequency argument $\omega_m$ is omitted for brevity. The spectra are left unnormalized because normalization cancels in the ratios below. To reduce variability between individual windows, the instantaneous spectra are averaged recursively with exponential weighting [4], following the modified-periodogram approach of [3]. review: Introduced the role of short-time spectra before the window settings, clarified the transform-to-spectrum and recursive-averaging sequence, and connected the monitored band to the following identification method. The preserved text says the first complete window initializes the average, but the displayed recursion does not specify its initial value.
